findings.element: Every uppercase Geist Mono micro-label — .b-where, .b-unit, .b-todayLabel, .b-measureHead, .b-origin, .b-date, .b-grabWord, .b-hiddenMark, .b-behindLabel, .b-behindCount, .b-behindDate, .b-behindState, and the two footer strings
findings.problem: Driven at 1440 on owner-flight, 34 of the 39 uppercase elements on the screen render at one byte-identical specification: 11px / Geist Mono / 400 / letter-spacing 1.76px (0.16em) / fore at 0.62. A section head (BEHIND YOU), a fact (SAT 1 AUG), a unit (DAYS), a time anchor (TODAY IS 16 JULY), a state (HIDDEN FROM GUESTS), an action (EDIT), a provenance stamp (KEPT BY ORLA) and the product wordmark (SIGNAL TIMELINE) are the same typographic object. The tracking ladder ships three values for this tier — --track-label 0.16em, --track-labelWide 0.20em, --track-data 0.04em — and the surface spends one of them on almost everything. The consequence is that the whole sub-15px layer is a single flat plane of caps: a reader scanning the phone has to READ each label to learn whether it is a heading, a value, a control or furniture, which is exactly the work a type system exists to remove. This is the single thing holding this seat below 9.5.
findings.fix: Split the micro tier into three declared roles across shell.css and b.css, using ladder values that already exist and introducing no size, weight or hue. (1) SECTION HEAD — and only the strings that open a region: .b-measureHead, .b-behindLabel, .b-todayLabel. Keep 11px/400 uppercase, move to --track-labelWide (0.20em), and make uppercase EXCLUSIVE to this role. (2) DATA — .b-date, .b-behindDate, .b-behindCount, .b-unit, .b-origin, .b-away. Drop text-transform to none (sentence case, 'Sat 1 Aug'), move to --track-data (0.04em), keep 11px mono; figures and dates then read as values rather than as headings and gain back roughly 12 percent of their line width. (3) STATE AND PROVENANCE — .b-hiddenMark, .b-behindState, the kept-by line, the footer wordmark. Keep 11px mono uppercase at --track-label but drop one step down the ink ladder so they sit visibly behind both roles above. Leave .b-grabWord (EDIT) at role 3's tracking but keep its underline, so the only underlined micro-string on the surface is the only pressable one. Then add an audit.mjs assertion that no more than three distinct strings on any state share the section-head spec — the rule that keeps the tier from re-collapsing when Home, Notes and Tasks inherit it.

findings.element: --track-display on .b-num (148px and 96px), .b-ogNum (64px) and .b-dayCount ('Today', 96px, weight 600); --track-title on .b-pressTitle (48px) and .b-emptyTitle (64px)
findings.problem: Measured across seven state and width combinations, --track-display renders at a flat -0.045em on 64px, 96px and 148px — a 2.3x size span on one value — and --track-title at a flat -0.035em on 48px and 64px. Tracking is an optical correction, not a constant: the em value that is right at 148px is over-tight at 64px. The specific casualty is the wedding morning. .b-dayCount is the one place the count's slot holds a WORD rather than a figure, and 'Today' is set at 96px / weight 600 / -0.045em — a value calibrated for two lining digits, which have no letterfit problem, applied to letters that do. In the rendered frame the o tucks under the arm of the T and the o-d and d-a pairs close to near-contact. On the frame with more feeling in it than any other in the product, the headline is optically crashed.
findings.fix: Grade the two display steps by size rather than by role name, and split figures from letters. Replace the single --track-display with three size-bound values in shell.css: --track-display-148 -0.05em, --track-display-96 -0.04em, --track-display-64 -0.032em, applied by the class that carries each size (.b-num at desk, .b-num at phone, .b-ogNum). Do the same for title: --track-title-64 -0.038em on .b-emptyTitle, --track-title-48 -0.032em on .b-pressTitle. Then give .b-dayCount its own value: because it is letters at weight 600, set it one full step looser than the figure at the same size, -0.03em, and keep --lead-display 0.9. Record the split in LANGUAGE.md's Tracking row as 'one value per size, and figures track tighter than letters at the same size' so the next product inherits the rule and not just the numbers.

findings.element: .b-date on every moment row — the mono date rail on owner-flight, phone, desk, day and print
findings.problem: The day figure is unpadded, so in a monospaced column 'Sat 1 Aug', 'Sat 8 Aug' and 'Sat 5 Sep' sit one cell to the left of 'Sat 22 Aug', 'Sat 29 Aug' and 'Sat 19 Sep'. The month abbreviation therefore steps in and out by one character cell — about 8.4px at 11px plus 0.16em — down the whole rail. It is visible in the 1440 owner frame and in the 390 guest frame, which is the screen the company is judged on. Mono was chosen here precisely so figures form a column; unpadded days spend that choice and buy nothing. It is the one place on the surface where a design whose entire thesis is that alignment carries meaning is not aligned.
findings.fix: In the date formatter in render-b.js, pad a single-digit day with U+2007 FIGURE SPACE — mono-cell width, and unlike U+00A0 it will not be trimmed or collapsed: emit 'Sat<U+2007>1 Aug' rather than 'Sat 1 Aug'. Strip the figure space when composing the row's aria-label and the printed sheet's text so screen readers and copy-paste still get 'Sat 1 Aug'. Apply the same padding to .b-behindDate on the past rail. Then assert it in interaction-check.mjs: measure the x of the month substring on every .b-date on owner-flight and require a single distinct value.

findings.element: The whole sans tracking ladder as it runs on the print state and any paper ground — .b-num -0.045em, .b-when -0.03em, .b-title -0.03em, body -0.015em, all identical to their ink-ground values
findings.problem: The system's best idea is the --fore / --back inversion: flip the ground in nine lines rather than maintain a parallel stylesheet. But tracking does not survive the flip unchanged. Light letterforms on a dark ground bloom optically and want slightly MORE letterfit; dark letters on white do not bloom and want less. Measured on the print state, every value is byte-identical to the screen: the 148px keepsake numeral runs -0.045em on paper and the 15px body runs -0.015em. The keepsake is the artifact that gets kept, and it is set with a screen's letterfit. Neither gate can see this, because both grounds pass the same numeric ladder check.
findings.fix: Add one ground-conditional block in shell.css beside the --fore/--back inversion, redefining only the sans tracking steps on paper, one notch looser at the top and one notch tighter at the bottom: under [data-ground="paper"] set --track-display -0.038em, --track-title -0.03em, --track-head -0.024em, --track-body -0.008em, leaving the mono steps (--track-label, --track-labelWide, --track-data) untouched because mono letterfit is not optical. Document it in LANGUAGE.md's Tracking row as the second axis: 'one value per size, per ground.' Cost is one block plus a re-render of the print PDF; no size, weight or hue moves.

findings.element: The share URL string on the publish state (13px Geist Mono) at 768x1024
findings.problem: Swept across 390 / 768 / 1280 / 1440 on eleven states, exactly one widow survives: at 768 the share URL wraps to two lines with the second line at 6 percent of the first — roughly three characters of the slug hanging alone under a full line. It clears the gate because the widow assertion measures only .b-note and .b-stepRead, on owner-editing, at 1280. The publish state is where the owner reads the link back to check it before sending, and a three-character orphan reads as a rendering fault rather than as a wrap.
findings.fix: Give the URL an explicit break policy rather than leaving it to the default: on the class carrying the share URL set overflow-wrap: anywhere, and constrain the element to a max-width in ch that is an integer fraction of the slug length so the two lines come out near-even — at 13px mono the string is 61 characters, so max-width: 32ch produces 32 + 29 rather than 58 + 3. Then extend the widow assertion in interaction-check.mjs to run over every text-bearing element on all eleven states at 390 / 768 / 1280 / 1440 with the same 0.25 floor, so this class cannot come back at a width nobody screenshots.

biggestWin: The one thing holding this seat below 9.5 is that the sub-15px tier has collapsed into a monoculture — 34 of 39 uppercase strings on the owner's screen render at one identical 11px / mono / 400 / 0.16em / 0.62 specification, so a section head, a date, a unit, a state, an action and the wordmark are typographically the same object and the reader must read every label to learn what kind of thing it is; the fix needs no new size, weight or hue, only the three tracking values the ladder already ships — 0.20em for section heads alone, 0.04em sentence-case for data, 0.16em one ink step down for state and provenance — which is polish plus one gate assertion, roughly half a day, after which everything else this seat can prove (display tracking graded by size, letters tracked looser than figures at the same size, the month column padded to align, one tracking notch off on paper) is another half day of the same kind of work.
